title: The Share of the Measured Balance a Paydown Is Taken At
content:
The share at which a paydown is taken on an Employee Meal Account is banded on how long the spending restriction has stood and on how lately charges have been accrued. The escalated paydown share is 75 percent and the eased paydown share is 30 percent.

**Clause.** Where the account has stood restricted for longer than the grace days printed against the plan and two or more charges have been accrued on it in the two calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, the required share is the escalated paydown share. Where the account has stood restricted for no longer than those grace days and no charge has been accrued on it in the two calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, the required share is the eased paydown share. Where neither holds, the required share is the reinstatement share printed against the plan.

## The bands

| Days the restriction has stood | Charges accrued in the two calendar months running back from the day the account is worked | The required share |
|---|---|---|
| Longer than the printed grace days | 2 or more | 75 percent |
| The printed grace days or fewer | None | 30 percent |
| Any other combination | Any | The reinstatement share printed against the plan |

## The grace days this reads, plan by plan

| Meal plan | Grace after the arrears threshold is passed |
|---|---|
| Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account | 0 calendar days |
| Prepaid Declining Balance Account | 0 calendar days |
| Payroll Deduction Meal Account | 10 calendar days |
| Subsidized Daily Allowance Account | 7 calendar days |
| Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account | 0 calendar days |
| Executive Dining Charge Account | 21 calendar days |

## Points of judgement

The two bands pull in opposite directions and neither can be reached by the other's facts: the escalated band needs a long-standing restriction *and* recent charging, the eased band needs a short-standing restriction *and* no charging at all in the two calendar months running back from the day the account is worked. A restriction standing exactly the printed grace days is not longer than them, so it can only reach the eased band or the fall-through.

*Hypothetical illustration.* On a plan printing 7 calendar days of grace, an account restricted for 30 days with 3 charges in the two calendar months running back from the day the account is worked is taken at 75 percent; the same account restricted for 5 days with no charges in that stretch is taken at 30 percent; restricted for 30 days with no charges, it falls to the reinstatement share printed against its plan.
